title: Stall correlation decomposition scan
content:
Summary:
This note captures the results of a targeted sweep to decompose and correlate short-duration GPU stalls observed in production traces. Goal was to identify whether stalls are dominated by (a) kernel-side resource contention, (b) async-copy / DMA phasing, or (c) runtime rendezvous (batcher handoff / queue swaps). We used a mix of Nsight timeline captures, NVTX-instrumented workloads, and per-kernel occupancy sampling to build a correlation matrix between stall clusters and candidate causes.

Why this matter:
- Tail-latency spikes in 99.9th have been observed across several microbatch sizes.
- Known mitigations (slightly larger microbatch, stream-priority heuristics) reduce frequency but not root cause.
- Understanding dominant cause lets us pick policy: kernel fusion, copy prefetch windows, or queueing backpressure.

Experiment setup:
- Model: distilled-medium-decoder (50M to 300M variants) with KV-cache enabled.
- Hardware: G5 (A10G-like) cluster with PCIe NVMe staging; some runs on NVLink-enabled hosts for comparison.
- Workload: synthetic fanout of short/long sequences (mean 64, 5% > 512) to reproduce heavy variability.
- Capture tooling: Nsight Systems (timeline events), NVTX markers around 1) batch-serialize, 2) enqueue-to-kernel, 3) kernel-start/end, 4) async-copy start/end.
- Additional probes: per-kernel SM occupancy via cupti-derived sampler at 1ms resolution; host-side queue depth histogram (0..32).

Key observations (high level):
1) Stall clusters are short (0.4ms - 3ms) and often co-occur with async-copy bursts but not always.
2) There are two dominant shapes in the kernel timeline: a) long-run kernels with short pre/post gaps, and b) short kernels with intermittent gaps that align with host queue drain events.
3) NVLink hosts show fewer copy-coincident stalls but a similar incidence of short gaps inside long kernels, suggesting intra-GPU contention independent of DMA path.

Correlation decomposition results:
- Method: Enumerate each stall instance (timeline hole longer than 0.3ms) and annotate with binary flags: (DMA_nearby, queue_swap, high_occupancy_transition, kernel-launch-congestion). Compute pairwise co-occurrence counts and normalized pointwise mutual information (PMI) to find non-random associations.
- Results (normalized PMI rank):
  * queue_swap <-> short-kernel-reappear: PMI 2.9 (strong) -- many stalls coincide with a host-side batcher swap where an inflight microbatch is handed to a different stream.
  * DMA_burst <-> 0.4-1.2ms stalls: PMI 1.7 (moderate) -- copies occasionally preempt kernel progress on PCIe hosts but not on NVLink.
  * occupancy-transition <-> 2-3ms stalls: PMI 2.1 -- kernel hot-set changes (change in active warps due to dynamic length scheduling) align with longer stalls.
  * kernel-launch-congestion alone has low PMI, indicating it's usually collateral with queue swaps.

Deep-dive examples (from Nsight captures):
- Case A (queue swap): timeline shows stream0 kernel completes, NVTX mark 'handoff' at t=+120us, next kernel scheduled on stream1 doesn't start for 1.6ms. Host-side logs show batcher popped a head-of-line item while a background housekeeping thread ran.
- Case B (DMA coincident): async-copy (host->device) peaks shortly before a 0.8ms hole on PCIe instance; cupti counters show a burst in L2 cache miss traffic, suggesting copy-induced bus congestion. Same workload on NVLink had reduced rate of these holes.
- Case C (occupancy transition): within a large decoder kernel the active-warp count drops then ramps up across a 2.3ms quiet window; correlated with dynamic branching inside kernel on long sequences (KV-cache path differences).

Small numeric results (representative):
- Total stalls sampled: 18,300 over 4h of steady load.
- Distribution: 56% < 1ms, 34% 1-2ms, 10% >2ms.
- Attribution by highest-PMI cause: queue_swap 45%, DMA 22%, occupancy_transition 27%, unclear 6%.

Implications for mitigations:
1) Queueing policy: the largest single win likely comes from reducing queue_swap-induced handoffs. Recommendations: implement soft handoff (allow a short pin period where microbatches keep stream affinity until kernel exit) or increase batcher backoff to avoid mid-kernel reassignments. Expected impact: reduce ~45% of short stalls.
2) DMA prefetch window tuning: for PCIe hosts, shift prefetch to earlier or opportunistic prefetch epochs (when host queue depth is low) to avoid overlapping heavy L2 traffic. On NVLink, deprioritize.
3) Kernel-level: add low-cost checks for occupancy phase transitions; if heavy branching detected, try splitting the kernel into two stable phases (fusion point) to avoid expensive warp wake/shuffle thrashing. This is higher engineering cost but addresses the 27% occupancy-transition class.

Quick wins and experiments to run next:
- Implement a short pin-time heuristic in the batcher (config flag) and run an A/B for 24h against baseline. Metric: reduction in 99.9th token latency and stall count.
- Run conditional prefetch offset: if queue_depth > X, delay prefetch by Y ms. Run on PCIe hosts only. Metric: correlation between async-copy bursts and stalls should drop.
- Instrument kernel to emit coarse-phase NVTX markers for hot paths so we can validate occupancy-transition detection without full kernel rewrite.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are some handoffs originating outside runtime (orch heartbeat, SRE agent)? We need to correlate host process traces with batcher events more tightly.
- The PMI method highlights associations but not causality; there may be a hidden confounder (e.g., GC or host checkpoint I/O).
- Some stalls (~6%) remain unattributed — propose enabling full system capture for a narrower 15-minute window to see host-side interrupts and driver activity.

Notes on instrumentation and commands used:
- Nsight Systems capture: nsight-sys profile --trace-gpu=on --capture-range=timerange:1.0s-61.0s --output=scan-export.qdrep
- NVTX: surrounding enqueue and handoff points with nvtxRangePushA / Pop and custom payloads: "batcher:enqueue", "batcher:handoff", "asynccopy:start", "asynccopy:end"
- cupti sampler: built with 1ms resolution; sample types: active_warps, sm_efficiency, l2_miss_rate
- Host queue histogram: lightweight agent increments atomically on enqueue/dequeue with periodic dump to logs every 100ms.

Appendix — quick checklist for rollouts:
- [ ] Add batcher pin_time config and feature flag.
- [ ] Implement host-side prefetch gating based on queue_depth.
- [ ] Add NVTX phase markers to decoder kernels (experimental build).
- [ ] Schedule full-system 15m capture on one PCIe and one NVLink host.

References / links:
- JIRA-INF-4921: "tail-latency stalls investigation"
- PR #2873: prototype batcher pin-time patch (WIP)

Author notes (notes-to-self style):
- Keep captures short and focused; QDREP files are huge. Trim to 60s windows around anomalous spikes.
- When computing PMI use Laplace smoothing (k=1) to avoid infinite scores for rare co-occurrences.

If reviewers want quick reproducer: I can share the synthetic load spec and a 2-node reproducible script. Tag me (Asha) in the ticket and I will hand off the artifacts.
